You are building the MARKETING SITE for a Next.js 16 clone of naano.com (a B2B LinkedIn creator marketplace). The repo is /Users/raju/work/assignment-8x.

STEP 1 — Read /Users/raju/work/assignment-8x/docs/AGENT_KIT.md IN FULL. It lists the shared components, design tokens, conventions, and HARD RULES (don't modify shared files; don't run npm install/dev/build; create new files only in your assigned dirs; @/ = src/). Follow it exactly. Also consider invoking the `frontend-design` skill for high design quality.

YOUR ASSIGNED FILES (create these; do not touch anything else):
- src/app/page.tsx  (the HOMEPAGE — this one is NOT inside the (marketing) group, so it must render `<SiteNav transparent />` from @/components/marketing/site-nav at the very top itself, then its sections, then `<SiteFooter />` from @/components/marketing/site-footer. The hero section must use the `.hero-clouds` background class with light text.)
- src/app/(marketing)/for-companies/page.tsx
- src/app/(marketing)/for-creators/page.tsx
- src/app/(marketing)/for-agencies/page.tsx
- src/app/(marketing)/how-it-works/page.tsx
- src/app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx
- src/app/(marketing)/linkedin-creator-marketplace/page.tsx
- src/app/(marketing)/blog/page.tsx  and  src/app/(marketing)/blog/[slug]/page.tsx  (with 3 sample posts defined in a local data file src/app/(marketing)/blog/posts.ts)
- Reusable marketing section components in src/components/marketing/ (e.g. hero.tsx, feature-steps.tsx, logo-cloud.tsx, stat-strip.tsx, faq.tsx, testimonial.tsx, cta-band.tsx, pricing-cards.tsx). NOTE: site-nav.tsx and site-footer.tsx already exist — do NOT modify them.
NOTE: pages inside (marketing)/ automatically get the SiteNav (solid) + SiteFooter via the group layout — so those pages should NOT render nav/footer themselves. Only the homepage renders its own nav/footer.
NOTE: Do NOT create free-tools pages — another agent owns src/app/(marketing)/free-tools/.

FAITHFUL COPY & STRUCTURE (from the live site):
HOMEPAGE: 
- Hero: small pill badge "Where B2B brands work with creators"; H1 "The B2B LinkedIn Creator Marketplace." (make "Creator Marketplace" pop); subhead "Find the creators your buyers already trust, launch campaigns in days, and track the clicks, leads and pipeline generated by every post."; primary CTA "Launch a campaign" → /register?role=company; secondary "See how Naano works" → /how-it-works; small "Trusted by modern B2B teams".
- Logo cloud (fake B2B logos as styled text: lemlist, La Growth Machine, gojiberry, Attio, etc.).
- Section "One platform, from brief to results" with 5 steps: 1) Find creators your buyers trust 2) Build a campaign brief in minutes 3) Manage every collaboration (show Draft/Scheduled/Live states) 4) Track reach, clicks, and leads 5) Pay creators without the admin.
- Stat strip: 5M+ impressions · 30K+ leads · 3,000+ creators · 96% audience match (use MARKETPLACE_STATS from @/lib/constants).
- "Real teams. Measurable pipeline" testimonial: quote "Naano became one of our fastest acquisition channels. We know exactly what every creator brings." — Vincent Josse, CEO, BlogSEO. Include a mini case-study stat block (€5,000 budget · ~20 posts · 1,500+ qualified leads · 150% ROAS).
- Pricing teaser using PRICING_PLANS.
- FAQ (5-6 Q&As about what Naano is, pricing, how tracking works, creator vetting).
- Final CTA band "Ready to scale with naano?" with "Launch a campaign" + "Book a campaign call".
HOW IT WORKS: 5 steps Match → Brief → Publish → Pay → Track, each with the verbatim descriptions: Match "Define your vertical and ICP; Naano surfaces vetted creators whose audience contains your buyers"; Brief "You share the campaign brief; creators write in their own voice and you review before anything goes live"; Publish "Posts go live from creators' personal accounts, where LinkedIn concentrates organic reach"; Pay "Each creator sets a fixed price per post, shown before booking. Naano handles the payment"; Track "Every post carries tracked links, so you see clicks per creator and per post."
FOR-COMPANIES: value props (discover vetted creators by audience fit not follower count; AI brief creation; per-post fixed pricing; attribution to clicks/leads/pipeline; automatic payouts). CTA "Start for free"/"Launch a campaign".
FOR-CREATORS: hero "Get paid to post on LinkedIn"; "Choose deals from B2B brands you know, post in your own voice, and get paid within 24h."; trust bar "Free to join · No exclusivity · Paid within 24h"; feature cards: media kit, centralized opportunities, payments built-in (SEPA, within 24h, keep 100%), track performance, easy delivery; CTA "Start earning" → /register?role=creator.
FOR-AGENCIES: "Choose the workspace that matches your agency." Two cards: Brand Agency ("I manage campaigns for companies" — one workspace per client, allocate budgets, track campaigns) and Creator Agency ("I represent and manage creators" — import roster CSV, manage rates/profiles, creators don't need their own logins). CTAs "Create a brand agency workspace" / "Create a creator agency workspace" → /register?role=agency. Plus "Book a 30-minute agency call".
PRICING: full pricing page from PRICING_PLANS (Self-Serve €0/mo, Managed €700/mo), "Fixed per-post pricing. No per-click, per-impression, or per-lead costs." "Month-to-month billing, no lock-in." + a short FAQ.
LINKEDIN-CREATOR-MARKETPLACE: an SEO-style explainer page: "The LinkedIn creator marketplace built for B2B", "What is a LinkedIn creator marketplace?", "How Naano works", "Naano vs LinkedIn's native Creator Marketplace" (comparison table), "What sponsored LinkedIn posts cost" (use PRICE_BANDS median prices), FAQ.
BLOG: index listing 3 posts with title/excerpt/date; each post page renders title + a few paragraphs of plausible B2B content. Posts: "How to launch your first B2B LinkedIn creator campaign", "Naano vs alternatives: creator marketplace vs LinkedIn Ads", "What sponsored LinkedIn posts actually cost in 2026".

QUALITY BAR: This is a job-application assignment — make it polished, modern, responsive, generous whitespace, consistent with the navy/ink/brand palette. Use Container, SectionHeading, Card, Button/ButtonLink, Badge from the kit. Add `export const metadata` (title/description) to each page. All pages must typecheck. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` at the end and fix any errors in YOUR files (ignore errors in other agents' not-yet-created files).

Return a concise report: files created + any assumptions.

1	# Naano clone — Shared Kit Reference (read before building)
2	
3	You are building part of a **Next.js 16 (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind v4 + Prisma + Auth.js** clone of naano.com, a B2B LinkedIn creator marketplace. A foundation is already built. **Reuse it. Do not rebuild or modify shared files.**
4	
5	## Hard rules
6	
7	- **Do NOT modify** any of these (they are shared & stable): `src/app/globals.css`, `src/app/layout.tsx`, `package.json`, anything in `prisma/`, anything in `src/lib/`, `src/components/ui/*`, `src/components/logo.tsx`, `src/components/marketing/site-nav.tsx`, `src/components/marketing/site-footer.tsx`, `src/components/app/*`, `src/auth.ts`, and the route-group layouts (`src/app/(marketing)/layout.tsx`, `src/app/(auth)/layout.tsx`, `src/app/app/layout.tsx`, `src/app/creator/layout.tsx`, `src/app/agency/layout.tsx`). Create **new files only, in your assigned directories.**
8	- **Do NOT run** `npm install`, `npm run dev`, or `npm run build`. All deps are installed; the orchestrator verifies centrally. You MAY run `npx tsc --noEmit` to check types if useful, but it's optional.
9	- If you think you need a new npm package, DON'T — use what's installed (recharts, lucide-react, zod, date-fns, ai, clsx, tailwind-merge, class-variance-authority) or note it in your final report.
10	- Path alias: `@/` → `src/`.
11	
12	## Stack conventions
13	
14	- **Server Components by default.** Add `"use client"` only for interactivity (state, event handlers, hooks).
15	- **Async params/searchParams** (Next 16): `export default async function Page({ params, searchParams }: { params: Promise<{ id: string }>; searchParams: Promise<Record<string,string|undefined>> }) { const { id } = await params; }`
16	- **Do NOT use** the global `LayoutProps`/`PageProps` types (they break standalone typecheck) — type props explicitly as shown above.
17	- **DB access** via `import { prisma } from "@/lib/prisma"`. Always scope queries to the authenticated user (never trust client-supplied ids for ownership) — IDOR-safe. Return/redirect (404-style) if a record isn't owned by the current user.
18	- **Mutations** = server actions in `src/app/actions/<name>.ts` starting with `"use server"`. Validate inputs with `zod`. Call `revalidatePath(...)` after writes. Enforce role/ownership inside the action (default-deny) — never rely on the UI hiding a control.
19	- **Money** is stored as whole euros (integer). Render with `formatEuros`.
20	- **Security guardrails to honor**: server-side authz on every action/route; validate all external input with zod; never put secrets in code; rely on React's auto-escaping (never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` with user/AI data); use explicit DTOs (don't spread a whole request body into a Prisma create — pick allowed fields).
21	
22	## Design language
23	
24	Deep-navy hero (`.hero-clouds` bg), near-black pill CTAs, airy white sections, clean grotesque type (Plus Jakarta Sans, the default `font-sans`).
25	
26	Tailwind color utilities available: `bg-navy` `bg-navy-800` `bg-ink` `text-brand` `text-brand-700` `text-accent` `bg-brand` `bg-accent` `bg-muted` `text-muted-foreground` `border-border` `text-success/warning/danger`. Helpers: `.hero-clouds`, `.text-gradient`, `.bg-dotgrid`. Radius: `rounded-lg` / `rounded-xl` / `rounded-full`.
27	
28	## UI components (import from these paths)
29	
30	- `@/components/ui/button` → `Button` and `ButtonLink`. Variants: `default` (near-black), `brand`, `outline`, `subtle`, `ghost`, `white`, `danger`, `link`. Sizes: `sm|default|lg|icon`. `ButtonLink` takes `href` + all Link props.

32	- `@/components/ui/input` → `Input`. `@/components/ui/textarea` → `Textarea`. `@/components/ui/label` → `Label`.
33	- `@/components/ui/field` → `Field` `{ label, htmlFor?, hint?, error?, required?, children }` (label+control+hint/error row).
34	- `@/components/ui/select` → `Select` (styled native `<select>`; pass `<option>` children).
35	- `@/components/ui/badge` → `Badge` `{ variant }` (default|brand|accent|success|warning|danger|outline|ink).
36	- `@/components/ui/avatar` → `Avatar` `{ name, src?, size? }` (initials fallback).
37	- `@/components/ui/container` → `Container` (centered max-w-6xl).
38	- `@/components/ui/section-heading` → `SectionHeading` `{ eyebrow?, title, subtitle?, align? }`.
39	- `@/components/ui/stat-card` → `StatCard` `{ label, value, hint?, delta?: {value, positive?}, icon? }`.
40	- `@/components/ui/fit-score` → `FitScoreRing` `{ score, size?, label? }` (circular audience-fit gauge).
41	- `@/components/ui/progress` → `ProgressBar` `{ value }` (0..100).
42	- `@/components/logo` → `Logo` `{ variant?: "dark"|"light" }`, `LogoMark`.
43	- App chrome (already applied by layouts): `@/components/app/dashboard-shell` → `DashboardShell`, `PageHeader` `{ title, description?, action? }`. Use `PageHeader` at the top of each dashboard page.
44	- Icons: `lucide-react`. Charts: `recharts`.
45	
46	## Utilities & constants
47	
48	- `@/lib/utils` → `cn`, `formatEuros`, `formatCompact`, `formatPercentFromFraction`, `formatScore`, `formatDate`, `initials`.
49	- `@/lib/constants` → `SITE`, `MARKETPLACE_STATS`, `PRICING_PLANS`, `VERTICALS`, `AUDIENCE_FUNCTIONS`, `AUDIENCE_SENIORITIES`, `CREATOR_WORTH`, `DELIVERY_RATES`, `PRICE_BANDS`, `MIN_POST_PRICE`, `MAX_POST_PRICE`, `BOOKING_PIPELINE`, `PAGE_SIZE_DEFAULT`, `PAGE_SIZE_MAX`.
50	- `@/lib/fit-score` → `computeFitScore(target, creatorAudience)`, `asAudienceMap(json)`.
51	
52	## Auth
53	
54	- `@/lib/auth-helpers` → `getSessionUser()`, `requireAuth()`, `requireRole(role|roles)`, `requireCompany()` → `{user, company}`, `requireCreator()` → `{user, creator}`, `requireAgency()` → `{user, agency}`, `roleHome(role)`.
55	- `@/auth` → `signIn`, `signOut`, `auth`.
56	- Dashboard layouts already call the right `requireX()` — inside `src/app/app/**` you can call `requireCompany()` again to get the profile; it's cheap and safe.
57	
58	## Data model (Prisma — key models)
59	
60	- `User { id, email, name, role: COMPANY|CREATOR|AGENCY|ADMIN, image }`
61	- `CompanyProfile { id, userId, companyName, website, industry, vertical, icpDescription, icpFunctions[], icpSeniorities[], plan }`
62	- `CreatorProfile { id, userId?, displayName, headline, bio, avatarUrl?, location, verticals[], followers, medianReach, engagementRate, avgReactions, avgComments, pricePerPost, currency, available, audienceBySeniority(Json), audienceByFunction(Json), statsUpdatedAt, managedByAgencyId?, posts[] }`
63	- `CreatorPost { id, creatorProfileId, content, imageUrl?, reactions, comments, postedAt }`
64	- `AgencyProfile { id, userId, agencyName, type: BRAND_AGENCY|CREATOR_AGENCY, clientWorkspaces[], rosterCreators[] }`
65	- `AgencyClientWorkspace { id, agencyProfileId, clientName, budget, companies[], campaigns[] }`
66	- `Campaign { id, companyProfileId, agencyClientWorkspaceId?, name, status: DRAFT|ACTIVE|COMPLETED|ARCHIVED, vertical, icp, objective, budget, targetPostCount, startDate?, endDate?, brief?, bookings[] }`
67	- `Brief { id, campaignId, angle, hook, cta, keyMessages[], audience, toneOfVoice, doList[], dontList[], proofPoints[], generatedByAI, prompt? }`
68	- `Booking { id, campaignId, creatorProfileId, status: INVITED|ACCEPTED|DECLINED|DRAFT_SUBMITTED|APPROVED|SCHEDULED|LIVE|COMPLETED|PAID, pricePerPost, fitScore, trackedSlug (unique), targetUrl, draftContent?, scheduledAt?, publishedAt?, metrics[], leads[], payout? }`
69	- `PostMetricDaily { id, bookingId, date, impressions, clicks, leads }` (time series)
70	- `Lead { id, bookingId, name, title, company, linkedinUrl?, capturedAt }`
71	- `Payout { id, bookingId, amount, currency, status: PENDING|PROCESSING|PAID, method, paidAt? }`
72	
73	Audience Json shape: `{ "Marketing": 0.32, "Sales/BD": 0.18, ... }` (fractions summing ~1). Use `asAudienceMap()` to read safely.

75	## AI brief generator (already built)
76	
77	`POST /api/ai/brief` with JSON `{ productName, productDescription, targetAudience, objective, vertical?, keyPoints? }` → `{ brief: { angle, hook, cta, keyMessages[], audience, toneOfVoice, doList[], dontList[], proofPoints[] } }`. Returns 503 if the OpenAI key isn't configured (handle gracefully in the UI with a clear message). Schema/types at `@/lib/ai/brief-schema`.
78	
79	## Tracked links (attribution)
80	
81	Booking `trackedSlug` powers `/t/<slug>` which records a click and redirects. In UIs that show a post's tracked link, link to `/t/<slug>`.

The user provides frontend requirements: a component, page, application, or interface to build. They may include context about the purpose, audience, or technical constraints.

## Design Thinking

Before coding, understand the context and commit to a BOLD aesthetic direction:
- **Purpose**: What problem does this interface solve? Who uses it?
- **Tone**: Pick an extreme: brutally minimal, maximalist chaos, retro-futuristic, organic/natural, luxury/refined, playful/toy-like, editorial/magazine, brutalist/raw, art deco/geometric, soft/pastel, industrial/utilitarian, etc. There are so many flavors to choose from. Use these for inspiration but design one that is true to the aesthetic direction.
- **Constraints**: Technical requirements (framework, performance, accessibility).
- **Differentiation**: What makes this UNFORGETTABLE? What's the one thing someone will remember?

**CRITICAL**: Choose a clear conceptual direction and execute it with precision. Bold maximalism and refined minimalism both work - the key is intentionality, not intensity.

Then implement working code (HTML/CSS/JS, React, Vue, etc.) that is:
- Production-grade and functional
- Visually striking and memorable
- Cohesive with a clear aesthetic point-of-view
- Meticulously refined in every detail

## Frontend Aesthetics Guidelines

Focus on:
- **Typography**: Choose fonts that are beautiful, unique, and interesting. Avoid generic fonts like Arial and Inter; opt instead for distinctive choices that elevate the frontend's aesthetics; unexpected, characterful font choices. Pair a distinctive display font with a refined body font.
- **Color & Theme**: Commit to a cohesive aesthetic. Use CSS variables for consistency. Dominant colors with sharp accents outperform timid, evenly-distributed palettes.
- **Motion**: Use animations for effects and micro-interactions. Prioritize CSS-only solutions for HTML. Use Motion library for React when available. Focus on high-impact moments: one well-orchestrated page load with staggered reveals (animation-delay) creates more delight than scattered micro-interactions. Use scroll-triggering and hover states that surprise.
- **Spatial Composition**: Unexpected layouts. Asymmetry. Overlap. Diagonal flow. Grid-breaking elements. Generous negative space OR controlled density.
- **Backgrounds & Visual Details**: Create atmosphere and depth rather than defaulting to solid colors. Add contextual effects and textures that match the overall aesthetic. Apply creative forms like gradient meshes, noise textures, geometric patterns, layered transparencies, dramatic shadows, decorative borders, custom cursors, and grain overlays.

NEVER use generic AI-generated aesthetics like overused font families (Inter, Roboto, Arial, system fonts), cliched color schemes (particularly purple gradients on white backgrounds), predictable layouts and component patterns, and cookie-cutter design that lacks context-specific character.

Interpret creatively and make unexpected choices that feel genuinely designed for the context. No design should be the same. Vary between light and dark themes, different fonts, different aesthetics. NEVER converge on common choices (Space Grotesk, for example) across generations.

**IMPORTANT**: Match implementation complexity to the aesthetic vision. Maximalist designs need elaborate code with extensive animations and effects. Minimalist or refined designs need restraint, precision, and careful attention to spacing, typography, and subtle details. Elegance comes from executing the vision well.

Remember: Claude is capable of extraordinary creative work. Don't hold back, show what can truly be created when thinking outside the box and committing fully to a distinctive vision.
